synthesis.brief_result: Ten new startups joined the list this week, which now has 50 companies in total. The strongest newcomer is Helical Fusion from Japan, which is building a fusion power plant to give the world clean power day and night, and it is bringing big industrial suppliers in as partners early. The trend of the week is space and defense hardware, with newcomers like ICEYE, Isar Aerospace and Helsing building satellites, rockets and drones for governments that suddenly need them.
gaps_result: Nobody applies the hard-science-plus-AI approach of AQEMIA, Cradle and CuspAI to agriculture or food, such as designing crop proteins or soil microbes for farmers in Africa or India.

The security startups (Island, Cyera, Upwind, Cymphony) all sell to large enterprises; a security product for small clinics, schools or local governments that cannot afford a security team is missing.
Frontline-worker software (Sona) and warehouse robots (Maven Robotics, Dexory) skip construction sites, where an AI that tracks progress and safety could combine both ideas.
Latin America and Africa barely appear outside fintech (Jeeves, Paymob) and BioLinker; a deep-tech startup there, such as local-language voice AI in the spirit of ElevenLabs and Loora, is open.
Medical AI like Nabla, Epsilon Health and Precision Neuroscience targets doctors and patients, but nobody builds AI aimed at nurses and care-home staff, who do much of the paperwork-heavy work.
